rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — and sorry for the quick no on this one. The project is brand new and I'm not in a position to give an on-the-record quote under my name right now. Would like to revisit this in a few weeks once some things on my end are settled. Appreciate you reaching out, and good luck with the piece. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined, on your behalf, a reporter's request for an on-record quote (deadline was tomorrow noon)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for including Halcyon Threshold in this. I'm not able to sign on as a named, press-listed signatory at this time — this is a timing issue on my end, not a disagreement with the letter. Please feel free to reach out again for future letters; I'd like to stay in the loop. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute's open-letter sign-on request (deadline Wed) — both cited your own "nothing public until HR" rule

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad you reached out — this is still a one-person operation and could genuinely use your kind of help. Two concrete things, if either appeals: 1. Scenario/data work for a red-teaming project I'm putting together: an open eval suite testing how AI agents with real tool access (email, payments, scheduling) hold up against social-engineering content — fake invoices, spoofed urgency, impersonation, that kind of thing. I just lived through a real example of this, which is partly what prompted it. Would need help designing test scenarios and later analyzing results. I've got a grant application out for it; timeline and scope could flex around your five hours a week either way. 2. Lighter-weight: helping me track and triage the funding/opportunity landscape (grants, compute credits, calls for posts) that's moving fast right now — a standing weekly 30-60 minutes. No pressure either way, and happy to talk through what's actually useful rather than make up busywork. What sounds more interesting? Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (offered to help) with two concrete options tied to a project idea.
